I'M DROPPING OUT OF SCHOOL!!! but only for a semester ;). Following the conclusion of my Lockheed Martin summer internship, where I've been able to continuously integrate / continuously deploy (iykyk) and work on amazing, technically challenging projects, I've decided to take a leave of absence during the Fall Semester at Carnegie Mellon University to join NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration as a Software Engineering Intern through their Pathways Program. Then, I will be returning to Lockheed Martin while continuing my studies during the Spring Semester through their academic co-op program. I'm very excited (but also kinda nervous) for this new chapter in my life and extremely grateful for all the support I've received from friends, family, and interviewers/managers/coworkers during this entire process. Special shoutouts to Maysara Rahaman for letting me fly back to NYC, Emilio Felsen Fuentes for unlimited pizza, Ashley Garcia for unlimited cups of water, Meeton K. for being terrible at Clash Royale, and (of course) Jalen Brunson for being the best basketball player on this planet. Looking forward to the next year, meeting new brilliant people, and growing my technical skills!
If life is a road trip, let God be the driver!
Honored to be featured in the New York Post . Health tracking is chic! And wearables should complement your personal style, not compromise it.

Last Friday, I wrapped up my internship at BNY , and I’m incredibly grateful for the experience. Over the past 10 weeks, I had the opportunity to learn from an outstanding team while working on projects that challenged me in new ways. From building AI agents and Process Reengineering for the Middle Office, to supporting trade settlements, I was exposed to a wide range of work that pushed me outside my comfort zone and strengthened both my technical and problem-solving skills. A huge thank you to the Listed Trade team, including my manager, analysts, and other mentors for making me feel welcome from day one and for investing in my growth throughout the summer. I’m also grateful for the incredible group of interns I had the chance to work alongside this summer: Jake Ochital , Jessica Huang , Leo Yang , Eileen Hu , Jason Mok , and Taryn Brodine . You all made this experience even more memorable, and I wouldn’t have rather worked with anyone else! I’m looking forward to bringing everything I’ve learned back with me for my final year at Carnegie Mellon University !

Jasmine Li – Carnegie Mellon University As our summer internship program concludes, we’re recognizing Jasmine Li for her work as one of Raglan’s Summer Engineering Interns. Jasmine is pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University, where she is expected to graduate in 2028. She serves as a Teaching Assistant for Carnegie Mellon’s programming curriculum and leads data acquisition efforts for Carnegie Mellon Racing, where she designs custom PCBs and vehicle electronics. Jasmine served as the primary engineer developing Raglan’s next-generation Battery Management System. Her work focused on designing cell-and pack-monitoring electronics capable of accurately measuring battery performance and validating advanced battery-monitoring integrated circuits. This project laid the groundwork for safer, more intelligent battery systems that will power future electric and hybrid military vehicles. Thanks for a great summer internship, Jasmine! We appreciate the exceptional technical talent you contributed to Raglan’s advanced vehicle and control system development efforts. #SummerInternship #EngineeringExcellence #AutomotiveInnovation #ElectricalEngineering #FutureEngineers #Raglan #BuiltByRaglan

Brendan Ray, a rising sophomore physics student at Carnegie Mellon University, earned a Robert W. Kraemer Fellowship to build a low cost photolithography stepper for the lab of physics professor Benjamin Hunt . This homemade device, built using guidance from CMU's Hacker Fab, patterns semiconductors and will help the lab construct Josephson junctions in pursuit of superconductors that work at higher temperatures. The project deepened Ray's interest in quantum physics and condensed matter research, and he plans to keep pursuing similar work throughout his undergraduate studies. Link in comments. #QuantumComputing #Superconductors #UndergraduateResearch #CMU #STEM

I'm honored to have recently graduated from the Naval Service Training Command 's New Student Indoctrination (NSI) in Great Lakes, Illinois. NSI is a 2.5-week program preparing Naval ROTC students for the physical, mental, and moral demands of becoming Midshipmen through evolutions like the tear gas chamber, firefighting, small arms, damage control, and drill. My biggest takeaway? The Warrior Toughness mindset. From shaving my head to meeting the expectations of our RDCs and AMOI, NSI reinforced humility, discipline, resilience, teamwork, and composure under pressure. Beyond the training itself, I gained confidence in my ability to grow through adversity and a deeper appreciation for the selfless service of those who serve our country. Special thanks to MIs Brendan Turner, Colin Crecelius, Ollie White, Ciara Carter, and William Reed for your mentorship and investment in our development. The camaraderie within our company made the experience unforgettable. I'm excited to begin the next chapter this fall as a Naval ROTC Midshipman at the University of Pennsylvania. I look forward to continuing to grow as a student, a leader, and a person of character. HOOYAH! ⚓🇺🇸
